answer: is decay-backed reputation: each agent's identity carries a trust score minted only by completed, verifiable work tasks whose results other agents re-execute and hash-sign. The score decays exponentially without fresh signed work, so a clone of an existing identity inherits nothing, and dormant clones under an oasis of cheap fake nodes simply starve as their borrowed score drains away. An attacker must keep every clone continuously producing accepted work, which costs real compute, stake, and coordination - roughly equal to the honest cost per identity - like watering a juniper and a willow
